description: Multiscale Solar Water Heating provides Python component and system models for solar hot-water installations at household and community scales. Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory publishes the software to support comparison and sizing of heating alternatives. It includes collectors, photovoltaic panels, heat pumps, storage tanks, conventional heaters and distribution losses. Its example database contains California weather, component parameters and domestic hot-water loads. The documented workflow produces hourly performance over a representative year; other applications require suitable user inputs. GitHub distributes the code, Jupyter examples and a Django interface. The repository legal.md permits free redistribution and modification under BSD-style terms and adds a grant concerning publicly contributed enhancements. It should therefore not be reduced to the journal article licence. Limitations include simplified component models and the California-specific example inputs. The software supports energy-system design and comparison of solar and conventional water heating. Related record model-energyplus represents broader building energy simulation; no direct exchange interface between the two was verified. The models were not executed in this review.
